plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE + power caveat + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 7 columns; 6 samples in metadata used for the 2-group comparison), unpaired, single batch. The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 workflow: QC of sample structure, a minimal low-count pre-filter, in-model median-of-ratios normalization, an explicit-reference-level design, a Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted independent filtering, and preranked fgsea enrichment against Hallmark and Reactome human gene sets found in the reference store. Because the smallest group holds only 3 replicates, the knowledge-base flags this as a low-power regime (R-0017/R-0094): both DESeq2 and edgeR find only a minority of true DE genes at this replicate count, mostly ones with large fold changes, so an edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check is added and the report states the power limitation explicitly rather than loosening thresholds to compensate. Enrichment runs the full ranked gene list (never a thresholded list) on the Wald statistic, per the disputed-rule resolution documented in each step's grounding.
